### Lost But Found
Author: Jessica Van Roekel
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/crosswalk-devo/lost-but-found-the-crosswalk-devotional.html
Passage: Luke 15:20
Points:
- Chasing after self-directed pleasures inevitably leads to spiritual emptiness and despair.
- Guilt and regret can deceive people into thinking they qualify only for partial forgiveness.
- God attentively watches and waits with tender compassion for wanderers to turn home.
- Repentant sinners who return are received with joy and fully restored as beloved children.

### Watching the Horizon for Your Prodigal
Author: Sarah Geringer
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/encouragement/encouragement-for-today-august-31-2020.html
Passage: Luke 15:20
Points:
- Watching a loved one wander away from faith brings deep heartbreak and weariness.
- Jesus gave this story to assure grieving families that God sees and shares their sorrow.
- God continuously scans the horizon, eagerly waiting to welcome home the lost.
- Waiting on God requires persistent faith and spiritual courage while outcomes remain unseen.

### Coming Home to the Father
Author: Vivian Bricker
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/crosswalk-devo/coming-home-to-the-father-the-crosswalk-devotional.html
Passage: Luke 15:21-24
Points:
- Severe trials and chronic suffering can tempt believers to doubt God's goodness and drift away.
- Renewing the mind with scriptural truth overcomes discouraging feelings of abandonment.
- Straying individuals often feel entirely unworthy of returning to a relationship with God.
- The Father responds to repentance not with rejection, but with lavish grace and celebration.

### The Embrace
Author: Mike DeVries
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/homeword/homeword-sept-28-2007-11555380.html
Passage: Luke 15:31-32
Points:
- The parable highlights two lost sons, including the embittered older brother who stayed home.
- The older brother allowed resentment and jealousy to blind him to his father's heart.
- Legalism leads people to demand rigid judgment instead of rejoicing in God's mercy.
- Believers are challenged to put away resentment and extend the Father's welcome to the repentant.
